entries.label: The Politics of Europe
entries.summary: Europe's economy improves but its politics worsen at every level.
entries.quote: Europe's economics are in substantially better shape than at the height of the Eurozone crisis. But the politics is now much worse.

entries.label: Russia
entries.summary: Russia remains a top risk after redrawing borders and entering a currency crisis.
entries.quote: Last year, we highlighted Russia as one of the top risks to global security--that was before Moscow carried out the most brazen redrawing of European borders since World War II, and then fell into a severe currency crisis.

entries.label: The Effects of China Slowdown
entries.summary: China's slowdown has spillover effects abroad even though Eurasia Group is optimistic about China itself.
entries.quote: We're quite optimistic about China this coming year.
entries.note: The printed opening sentence is optimistic; the risk is the external effect of slower Chinese growth.

entries.label: Weaponization of Finance
entries.summary: Washington uses financial tools such as sanctions as instruments of power.
entries.quote: The United States remains the world's only superpower, but Washington is now using its influence in important new ways.

entries.label: ISIS, Beyond Iraq and Syria
entries.summary: ISIS loses ground at its core but its reach spreads across the Middle East and North Africa.
entries.quote: In 2015, ISIS faces setbacks in its core bases in Iraq and Syria, but its military power remains significant, and its ideological reach will spread throughout the Middle East and North Africa.

entries.label: Weak Incumbents
entries.summary: Recently re-elected but weak incumbents weigh on key markets.
entries.quote: Political risk stemming from weak incumbents who recently won reelection will weigh on key markets in 2015.

entries.label: The Rise of Strategic Sectors
entries.summary: Business success depends more on governments.
entries.quote: In 2015, success and failure for business will depend increasingly on governments.

entries.label: Saudi Arabia vs. Iran
entries.summary: Saudi-Iran tension spikes and deepens the sectarian rift.
entries.quote: Saudi-Iran tensions will spike during 2015, worsening the Sunni-Shia sectarian rift across the region.

entries.label: Taiwan/China
entries.summary: Cross-strait relations deteriorate after the DPP's local-election win.
entries.quote: Relations between China and Taiwan will deteriorate sharply in 2015 following the opposition Democratic Progressive Party's (DPP's) landslide victory over the ruling nationalist party in November's local elections.

entries.label: Turkey
entries.summary: Turkey's troubles continue despite lower oil prices.
entries.quote: For the second year in a row, Turkey makes our list. Lower oil prices have been good news for this country, but that's about all that's going well.

entries.label: Asia Nationalism
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects Asia's key leaders to avoid foreign conflict despite nationalism.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: The Islamic State
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect a viable ISIS state in 2015.
entries.quote: But the Islamic state that the group would create will not prove viable in 2015
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Petrostates
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect low oil prices to destabilise authoritarian oil producers quickly.
entries.quote: That will not be the case.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Mexico
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects Pena Nieto to recover through economic reform.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.
